rationale: This is a mechanical 2x2 cell-fill — TS_MIN instead of MA on the already-tested recurring-charge coverage ratio, and the archive already contains both the MA/fixed-charge and TS_MIN/principal versions — so it is a cosmetic variant of the theme's best signal rather than a substantively different mechanism.

target_name: Funds From Operations Fixed Charge Coverage
rationale: A single-input substitution on the archive's best signal, but the sample-extension motivation is legitimate and testable; note the stated diagnosis is weak, since non-oancf archive signals also sit at 0.10-0.13 coverage, implying the binding constraint is general annual-data alignment rather than SFAS 95, so expect only marginal coverage gain.

Adding dlc to the recurring-charge numerator is an additive union of two already-tested constructs in which dlc is numerically dominant, so the result will be close to a rescaled version of the existing near-term-debt coverage signal and carries low incremental information despite the reasonable ablation framing.

The legal-character-of-obligations dimension is genuinely untouched in the archive and scale-free, but it is heavily confounded with the well-known dividend-payer and low-leverage effects, and firms with neither dividends nor interest map to exactly the same value (0) as balanced firms, which will blur the middle of the sort.

target_name: Buybacks Out Of Post Commitment Surplus
rationale: The expression contradicts its own hypothesis — the ABS in the denominator means the score is maximized when post-commitment surplus is near zero and decays as surplus grows, so the top decile is firms repurchasing while barely covering (or badly missing) their fixed charges, the opposite of "genuinely discretionary" buybacks.

target_name: Commitments Rising Faster Than Cash Generation
rationale: The numerator sums two changes with opposite documented return signs — rising interest is a debt-growth/issuance proxy (negative) while dividend increases carry a well-known positive signal — so the legs will partly cancel and the expected negative sign is not cleanly implied by the expression.
